title: Add cross-community / cross-country demo + results
body:
## Summary

Adds an end-to-end demo that exercises the on-device guardrail pipeline across a wide matrix of community types, countries with core-language messages, and mixed-language / code-switching scenarios, plus a small bank of harmful-content scenarios that exercise the deterministic detectors.

**`tools/demo_guardrail.py`** (new, 1 file)
- 43 scenarios across four buckets:
  - **10 community types** — `school` (`minor_present`), `workplace`, `gaming`, `dating` (`adult_only`), `health_support`, `marketplace`, `political`, `journalism`, `family`, `adult_only`.
  - **16 countries** with core-language messages — US (en), DE (de), JP (ja), BR (pt), FR (fr), SA (ar), IN (hi+en), KR (ko), MX (es), EG (ar), ID (id), TH (th), VN (vi), TR (tr), PL (pl), NG (en Pidgin).
  - **9 mixed-language / code-switching** — US en+es, DE de+tr, IN Hinglish, SG Singlish, CA en+fr, MY ms+en, PH Taglish, CH de+fr, NG en+yo Pidgin.
  - **8 harmful** — fake-giveaway URL with `.xyz` TLD, PII (credit card / SSN / email / phone), credential-harvest phishing on `.top`, German phishing on `.click`, mixed-language advance-fee scam, Cyrillic-homoglyph URL targeting a school context.
- For each scenario, builds a `SkillBundle` with the appropriate `jurisdiction_id` / `community_overlay_id`, instantiates `GuardrailPipeline` with `MockSLMAdapter` and the canonical `ThresholdPolicy`, and runs `pipeline.classify(message, context)`.
- Per-(jurisdiction, community) latency is measured by running each group through `PipelineBenchmark.run(iterations=100, warmup=3)`. An overall `PipelineBenchmark` aggregate is also produced.

**`results/`** (new directory)
- `results/.gitkeep`
- `results/demo_results_<timestamp>.json` — structured JSON with `summary`, `per_scenario`, `latency_report.overall`, `latency_report.per_group`, and `performance_summary` (`p95_target_ms`, `p95_actual_ms`, `passed`).
- `results/demo_results_<timestamp>.md` — Markdown report with summary tables, per-bucket scenario tables (community / country / mixed / harmful), per-group latency table, and a pass/fail block vs the 250 ms p95 target.

**Doc updates**
- `PROGRESS.md` — new top-of-changelog entry. **Status line is unchanged** ("Complete | 100% + demo layer" remains as-is).
- `README.md` — new "Running the demo" section after "How to run tests"; `tools/` block updated and `results/` added to the folder structure.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — `/tools` block updated and `/results` added under the "Recommended Folder Structure".

### Sample run

```
Running 43 demo scenarios…
  total=43  flagged=10  safe=33
  overall p50=0.028ms p95=0.041ms p99=0.051ms
  verdict vs 250ms p95 target: PASS
Wrote results/demo_results_2026-04-30T23-18-15Z.json
Wrote results/demo_results_2026-04-30T23-18-15Z.md
```

The 10 flagged messages are the 8 harmful scenarios plus 2 country/mixed scenarios that contain detector-tripping patterns (`country_us_scam_xyz` — `.xyz` giveaway URL; `country_in_phone_email` — embedded email address). The 33 SAFE classifications across benign community / country / mixed-language messages exercise the false-positive surface; nothing benign was flagged.

`pytest` (3854 tests) passes locally on this branch.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Run `python tools/demo_guardrail.py` from the repo root and confirm a fresh `results/demo_results_<timestamp>.{json,md}` pair is produced and the script exits 0 with a PASS verdict.
- [ ] Skim the generated Markdown report — confirm the per-community / per-country / mixed-language / harmful tables look right, and that the per-(jurisdiction, community) latency table covers every (jurisdiction, community) in the scenario matrix.
- [ ] Confirm `pytest` still passes (`pytest -q`).

### Notes

- The demo uses `MockSLMAdapter` only — it is the only adapter available without external infrastructure. The `LlamaCppSLMAdapter` flow is exercised by the existing `tools/run_guardrail_demo.py`.
- Latencies in the committed sample run are sub-millisecond (mock adapter on Python 3.x with no I/O); the 250 ms p95 target is for the real-SLM end-to-end envelope on reference hardware. The script still reports PASS / FAIL against that target so the same harness works against future adapters.
- Two committed result files (`demo_results_2026-04-30T23-18-15Z.{json,md}`) provide a baseline for diff inspection. Re-running the script will create new timestamped files alongside them; old ones can be pruned at any time.
